kind: tool comparison (TLSF), 2x2 factorial, all four arms from one binary, run at AuRUS's own search budget
kind_note: Counter's budget is a count of generations and AuRUS's is a count of individuals, so the two were never measured against a common currency. This campaign gives counter AuRUS's rule: stop at 1000 bred individuals, population 100, parallel 1, with generations 500 as a ceiling that must not bind. The 2026-08-14 head-to-head gave counter 10 generations at population 200, roughly twice the individuals.
question: What counter's anytime behaviour looks like against AuRUS's when both search the same number of individuals, and what the selection scheme and the status grading cost inside that budget.
endpoint: None registered. PLAN.md section 2 declares no primary endpoint, no alpha, no control arm and no decision rule. The deliverable is the six metrics of section 11: solutions, ideal_solutions, time_to_first_repair, time_to_first_ideal_repair, maximal_solutions and maximal_ideal_solutions.
decision_rule_firing: There is no decision rule to fire. PLAN.md section 2 registers none, and says so against the practice of every other plan in this archive, which do bind one. This field is filled rather than left blank because a blank here would read as an unfinished close. Every p-value in REPORT.md and in this file is POST-HOC and labelled as such at the point it is written: a test chosen after the curves are drawn describes this sample and tests no hypothesis, the contrast and the metric and the time cut all having been free when the analyst picked them.

arms.shared: termination individuals, max_individuals 1000, generations 500 (ceiling), population_size 100, parallel 1, weights 0.1/0.2/0.7, log metric, weakening screen off, accumulate_repairs on, monolithic repair mode

corpus: 25 families, seeds 0-29, 3000 runs; 24 of the 25 overlap AuRUS's archived corpus

verification.note: The five checks of PLAN.md section 12, run before anything was drawn from these rows.

1_stopped_by.detail: individuals on all 2685 manifests, generations on none. The 500-generation ceiling never bound; generations_run ran 25 to 31.

2_individuals_bred.detail: Exactly 1000 on every one of the 2685 manifests. Zero overshoot, where the between-slot check permits a small one.

3_ideal_solutions_join.detail: implies_ideal is 1403 of 3000 (46.8%) in the results CSV, so the endpoint is not flat zero and the curve join has a non-trivial target to agree with.

4_cost_off_own_rows.result: the plan's estimate was low by 2.77x
4_cost_off_own_rows.detail: Mean 1382.5 s a run against the 500 s PLAN.md section 13 assumed, median 296.0 s, max 7200.1 s. The campaign took 37.0 h against the estimated 13 h.

5_censored_count.detail: A censored run is a run directory holding accumulated/index.tsv with no run.json. Concentrated: humanoid-742 120/120, humanoid-531 93/120, pcar-v2-888 44/120, prioritized-arbiter-aurus 24/120, humanoid-503 20/120, full-arbiter-aurus 7/120, lift 7/120.

cost.note: 54.7% of the campaign's machine time went on runs that were killed at the 7200 s cap. A killed run writes no manifest and scores as a failure in every column of the results CSV, so that share bought no scored row. Only the accumulator, which flushes as it goes, records what those runs actually found.

caveats.post_hoc: Every p-value is post-hoc. See decision_rule_firing.
caveats.solution_means_two_things: counter's curve counts candidates that passed its output gate, flushed by the accumulator with sub-second timestamps. AuRUS's counts the running length of ga.solutions read off its per-iteration log line, which moves only at a generation boundary and is dated to the second. A like-for-like reading has to be taken at cuts coarse enough for both.
caveats.a_kill_is_not_symmetric: AuRUS writes its solution files in one batch when the run ends, so a run killed at the cap loses every one and can carry no verdict; counter's accumulator flushes as it goes, so a killed counter run keeps every candidate it found. The two biases run opposite ways: counter's kills score implies_ideal as zero, so humanoid-742 reads 0.000 on 120 of 120 killed runs, while AuRUS's kills drop out, so humanoid-503 left the comparison entirely on 30 of 30 killed runs. REPORT.md reads the head-to-head both ways and headlines neither.
caveats.aurus_rates_are_unfiltered: analyse_aurus_h2h.py scored a well-separation-screened implies_genuine from validation-av2.csv and validation-av3.csv. Neither file survives on either host, so the hit column is used as-is. The archived record of that screen is that it moved 2 of 25 family rates -- lift 0.167 to 0.300, lily11 0.900 to 0.833 -- so it is a small correction in an unknown direction rather than a negligible one.
caveats.paper_gaps: PLAN.md section 9 records three gaps between the AuRUS paper and its code -- the weights, the status ladder's six levels against the published five, and how an individual is counted. counter matches the code on all three, so the budget match is a code-level match and no claim here may be made against the paper's Table 2.

vendored_scripts.note: Verbatim copies, each verified with git hash-object. The four that ran the campaign are taken from ec0abe0; the five that scored and analysed it are taken from 59139e2, the analysis tip at close. score_curves.py there carries the survivor carry-forward that made the maximality pass 4.5x cheaper (8599c25), the bounded maximal call (22b78ad), the partial-curve write (96c3311) and the stop-on-abandon that ended the 752 retried cuts costing 48% of worker-hours (d4f8be4); analyse_matched.py carries the truncated-curve read (59139e2). analysis_lib.py is vendored because analyse_matched.py imports it, and both run as python3 scripts/<name>.py so sys.path[0] resolves against these copies.

owed: A pairwise-relation flag on `compare`, which would make the incremental maximal antichain reachable from a script. The curves here are scored by carrying each cut's survivors into the next, which is 4.5x cheaper than re-running `maximal` over the whole prefix -- 60.1M pairwise implication comparisons against 272.7M over this campaign's 546,282 accumulated candidates. The textbook algorithm is about 12x: keep one running antichain, test each arrival against it alone, remove what it dominates and discard it if anything dominates it. That needs an oracle answering whether one .tlsf file implies another, and neither binary exposes one although both compute it. `compare` walks the full repairs x ideals cross (src/compare.cpp:269-293) and then collapses it to the best relation per repair under the priority equivalent > stronger > weaker > incomparable > timeout, which is exactly what hides the domination the algorithm needs: a candidate stronger than one antichain member and weaker than another reports `strictly stronger`. `maximal` computes both directions per pair in compute_subsumed (src/filter/implication.cpp:39-42) and reports only the surviving antichain. So the smallest change is an output-format flag on `compare` printing every pair rather than the best, against a loop that already exists, rather than new logic in either binary. Not done here because the deployed 4.5x already took the pass from a day to a few hours, the remaining 2.7x is worth about four hours on a job that is now short, and a rebuild would put a third source commit into this file for an offline scoring binary.

A survivor-block skip in score_curves.py's maximality pass: 54.8% of the pairs each cut sweeps are survivor pairs the previous cut already found non-dominating, re-decided from cold in a fresh maximal process. The skip is exact and would roughly halve the pass, which is what would bring the 280 partial curves within the 900 s per-cut budget on most families other than humanoid-742.

A re-score of the 205 compare-undecided runs under 2defe77, should anything need humanoid-742's or humanoid-531's ideal curves; every other ideal count is a lower bound for the per-pair reason recorded in maximality_pass.compare_undecided_runs.
config_vintage: No entry is owed in the 'Config vintage' note of experiments/README.md. The three termination keys this campaign turns arrived at no-op defaults and no C++ default moved for it, so an archived config omitting them means exactly what it always meant.

reproduce: Check out ec0abe0, build the release preset, and drive it with this directory's vendored scripts/gen_configs.py using the command campaign.toml carries. The AuRUS side is not reproducible from this repository: it comes from that tool's own archive on av2, extracted by the two vendored aurus scripts into experiments/aurus-reference/, which is gitignored.

scoring_binaries.note: The offline pass that scored the two maximal metrics and the ideal join ran three binaries from the same branch: score_curves.py drives compare for the ideal relations and maximal for the antichain at each cut. The source of both was unchanged between ec0abe0 and the two perf commits named here, so a build from any commit in between is the same binary.
scoring_binaries.compare: ec0abe0 source (unchanged until 2defe77). The pass ran the pre-2defe77 compare throughout, so every ideal relation in curves-matched.csv comes from a compare that runs ltlfilt --simplify on each whole-spec query.
scoring_binaries.maximal: Two builds. 1956 of the 3000 curves come from the pre-d4f8be4 maximal, which ran ltlfilt --simplify on every query; 1044 come from d4f8be4, which skips that pass and gives SPOT black's budget, deployed on 2026-09-03 after the pass was measured at 95.6% of solver wall time (1153.7 s against 52.9 s for the decision itself) and a 40-file batch went from 304 s to 30 s with the same survivors. The two agree on all 264 cut-values of a 10-run sample once SPOT has black's budget; at the search's 500 ms budget 14 of 264 differed, every one an undecided query read as keep-both, which is why maximal.cpp raises it. The 256 partial curves the old build had produced were retired and re-scored under the new one.

maximality_pass.invocation: scripts/score_curves.py --maximality --cuts 20 --jobs 4 --maximal-timeout 900 --deadline-s 4500, one invocation per run directory, eight workers a host over a smallest-first queue, each worker pinned to four cores; av2 scored seeds 0-14 and av3 seeds 15-29, the campaign's own split.

partial_curves.meaning: score_curves.py abandons a cut whose maximal call exceeds the 900 s per-cut budget and, since 96c3311, writes the cuts it has rather than nothing. A partial curve ends before the run's last arrival and carries no marker of its own; analyse_matched.py (59139e2) detects one by that test and reads its cuts past the last computed one as undecided rather than carrying the last value forward. The bracketed count beside each maximal cell in analysis-output.txt is the number of runs so excluded at that cut.

compare_undecided_runs.meaning: compare exceeded the 600 s cap score_curves.py gives it, so the run has no candidate-to-ideal relation and ideal_solutions and maximal_ideal_solutions are blank at every cut. The analysis reports these as undecided and excludes them from those two metrics; they are not zeros. The same 205 runs are blank in both metrics, the join being one compare call per run.
compare_undecided_runs.cause_and_fix: The same ltlfilt --simplify pass. 2defe77 on this branch turns it off on compare's TLSF path and gives SPOT black's 20 s budget; over 26 runs, one per family, the new binary finished every run in at most 155 s, and on the 24 the old one also finished 17 outputs are byte-identical and 7 differ only where a pair the old binary reported as timeout is now decided, every one as incomparable, so no decided relation changed.
compare_undecided_runs.decision: Not re-scored. The 205 stand as undecided in the archive by decision on 2026-09-04, the cost of a re-score being a second maximality pass over the hardest families for a gain on two families the head-to-head already cannot read.
compare_undecided_runs.lower_bound: The old compare also left individual candidate-ideal pairs undecided inside runs it did finish (one humanoid-531 run read timeout on 79 of 95 pairs, one pcar-v2-888 run on 112 of 136), and an undecided pair counts as not ideal-implying. Every ideal count in the archive is therefore a lower bound. In the 26-run check none of those pairs became ideal-implying once decided.

maximality_pass.redundant_work_not_removed: 54.8% of the pairs each cut sweeps are survivor-against-survivor pairs already known non-dominating from the previous cut, re-decided from cold because each cut is a fresh maximal process. Removing them is exact and would roughly halve the pass; it is in owed.
